title: PGDR: Gradient Disagreement for Shortcut-Bias Detection
summary: Persistent Gradient Disagreement Reweighting discovers shortcut-conflicting examples without training group labels, by asking whether a hard example pushes the classifier in a different gradient direction than easy same-class examples.
abstract: Shortcut learning is an incorrect inductive bias: a model can perform well on average while relying on a feature that is predictive in training but not part of the intended concept. In Waterbirds, the intended label is bird type, but the shortcut is background. PGDR tests a mechanism-driven signal for discovering hidden groups without group supervision.

title: Jailbreaking Deep Models with Adversarial Image Attacks
summary: Evaluates how small L-infinity bounded perturbations collapse a pretrained ResNet-34, and whether those adversarial examples transfer to other architectures.
abstract: Image classifiers can be accurate on clean data but brittle under adversarial perturbations. This work quantifies that brittleness across one-step, iterative, patch-constrained and transfer attacks under an epsilon = 0.02 budget on a 100-class ImageNet-1K subset.

title: Beyond Natural Images: Cross-Domain Super-Resolution Benchmark
summary: Studies whether super-resolution models trained on natural images generalize to text and astronomical imagery, where natural-image priors break down.
abstract: Most reconstruction models are optimized around natural image priors: smooth gradients, dense textures, locally correlated edges. This benchmark compares EDSR, SwinIR and a diffusion upscaler across DIV2K, TextZoom and STAR to test whether those assumptions survive domain shift.

results.value: Natural-image quality did not predict cross-domain robustness

title: Parameter-Efficient RoBERTa Fine-Tuning with LoRA
summary: Adapts RoBERTa for AG News classification under a strict sub-1M trainable-parameter budget using LoRA adapters and knowledge distillation.
abstract: Full RoBERTa fine-tuning updates over 100M parameters. LoRA freezes the base model and trains small low-rank updates inside selected layers, making adaptation practical under tight compute budgets.

title: Improved ResNet for CIFAR-10 Classification
summary: A parameter-efficient ResNet-style classifier staying under a 5M parameter budget while holding high validation accuracy.
abstract: The main engineering idea is not simply to make the network deeper. The model combines progressive filter scaling, residual blocks, dropout, batch normalization, label smoothing and a OneCycleLR schedule to improve generalization under a compact parameter budget.
